identity.title: Debris Disks in the Scorpius-Centaurus OB Association Resolved by ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a CO(2-1) and 1240 $\mu$m continuum survey of 23 debris disks with spectral types B9-G1, observed at an angular resolution of 0.5$''$-1” with the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA).

targets.name: 24 Sco-Cen disks (e.g. HIP 73145, HIP 76310, HIP 84881, HIP 62657, HIP 79516)

evidence.quote: Distance to the star from *Hipparcos* parallax measurement (cite: lee07)

question.value: How prevalent is CO gas in ~10 Myr Sco-Cen debris disks, and what are the dust geometry, grain sizes and masses of the resolved disks?

evidence.quote: The sample was selected for large infrared excess and age $\sim$10 Myr, to characterize the prevalence of molecular gas emission in young debris disks.
This work makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00688.S.
Band 6 was utilized for all observations, with four dual-polarization spectral windows centered at frequencies of 230.6, 232.6, 245.4, and 247.4 GHz.

method.value: MIRIAD uvfit point source or elliptical Gaussian fits in visibility domain; resolved if major axis >3 sigma

evidence.quote: if the major axis length was measured with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $> 3\sigma$, we consider the disk spatially resolved

method.value: Model optically thin disk images (1 AU/pixel) sampled with uvmodel, chi2 compared to visibilities, MCMC for R_In, DeltaR, i, PA

evidence.quote: sample these synthetic images at the same baseline separations and orientations as the data using the MIRIAD task `uvmodel`

key_parameters.value: surface density power law p = 1 fixed

evidence.quote: we set $p = 1$

assumptions.value: i and PA fixed to CO-derived values for gas-rich disks

evidence.quote: we set best fit values of $i$ and $PA$ from fits to the CO J=2-1 line emission

fitting.value: Affine-invariant MCMC (emcee), chi2 likelihood in visibilities

evidence.quote: we utilize the affine-invariant Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting technique as described by (cite: good10) and implemented in Python as `emcee`
the values of $PA$ and $i$ that we derive are consistent with the previously determined geometry to within the uncertainties

analysis_steps.goal: Simultaneous SED and visibility fit for grain size and mass

method.value: Fix geometry; fit SED (lambda>5 um) plus visibilities with modified blackbody; add unresolved inner belt when needed

evidence.quote: we fix the geometry of the grain population responsible for the continuum emission from the outer disk and then perform simultaneous modeling of the ALMA visibilities and broad-band SED

key_parameters.value: beta = 0.8; rho = 2.7 g cm^-3; grain sizes 0.1-3000 um

evidence.quote: We assume $\rho = 2.7$ g cm$^{-3}$

assumptions.value: Compact astrosilicates (Draine 2003), Mie theory temperatures; Kurucz-Lejeune photosphere

evidence.quote: We assume that the composition of the grains is compact astrosilicates (cite: drai03) with characteristic grain size $a$.
we find that we need to also vary $a$ in order to successfully recreate the SED and visibilities (raw $\chi^{2}$ in Column ) as justified by the Akaike Information Criterion

validation.value: AIC significance of free grain size and inner belt (>10 sigma)

evidence.quote: these models are all significantly better than the models without an inner belt at the $> 10\sigma$ level
CASA reduction scripts for the ALMA data were provided by the staff at the North American ALMA Science Center (NAASC).

findings_qualitative.value: Gas-rich disks tend to have larger outer radii and smaller grains; no dust-mass difference

evidence.quote: The gas-rich debris disks exhibit preferentially larger outer radii in their dust disks, and a higher prevalence of characteristic grain sizes smaller than the blowout size.

claims.hypothesis: CO-rich debris disks are common around young intermediate-mass stars
claims.result: Three strong CO debris detections, all A stars, plus two tentative
claims.finding: Conditions around A stars favor CO survival or formation

evidence.quote: The three debris disks in our sample with strong CO detections are all around A stars

claims.hypothesis: Gas-rich disks are larger and have smaller grains
claims.experiment: Visibility and SED fitting of 12 resolved disks
claims.result: CO-rich disks are three of four largest outer radii; two of three with grains below blowout

evidence.quote: These results provide suggestive, although not conclusive, evidence that gas-rich disks may be preferentially more extended and contain smaller grains

claims.hypothesis: Gas-rich disks have larger dust masses

evidence.quote: there appears to be no correlation between the presence of substantial quantities of molecular gas and the dust mass inferred from continuum emission

why_this_method.value: Visibility-domain fitting because noise is well understood and CLEAN images lack well characterized uncertainties

evidence.quote: We carry out this analysis in the visibility domain because the noise is well understood (cite: schw78)

limitations_admitted.value: Low resolution prevents breaking R_Out/p degeneracy and resolving widths

evidence.quote: we are unable to break the degeneracy between $R_\mathrm{Out}$ and $p$ that arises in our modeling

referee_caveats_inferred: Fixed p, beta and grain density affect masses and grain sizes
